NE_2003.proof: The preceding extrema argument never used the range restriction on D; it therefore proves the same span inequality for every finite unrestricted background.

NE_THESIS.proof: Put a=x−1>y. For any finite D, max(D∪{a})<=max(D∪{x}) and min(D∪{a})>=min(D∪{y}), hence span(left)<=span(right). Equality can occur only with equal upper endpoints, so the (−span,max,min) tuple favors left. This covers every ranged background and every finite n.

VRC avoidance.proof: With no shared background, the left is homogeneous positive (span 0), while the right contains both a negative and a positive life (positive span); left wins.

DA_2003.proof: The same high-count and maximum argument allows C to be any finite nonempty mixture of positive levels, so it proves the 2003 weak edge as well.

DA_THESIS.proof: Every B life is above every A life. Therefore B contributes at least as many high lives as A; if tied, max(B)>max(A), and adding positive C cannot lower either tier.

ED.proof: If A's high-count tier exceeds B's, A wins immediately; if tied, max(A)=x>max(B).

GNEP.proof: With (u,y,n)=(4,3,1), after any shared E cancels in the high-count difference, left-minus-right is n+1[z>=4]−1[z+1>=4]>=0. It is strict except the only tie case n=1,z=3; there max(left)>=max(right) because x>=4 and B<=3. Thus the unbounded E and every finite z are covered.

VRC avoidance.proof: A contributes n high lives at z>=4; B is confined to 1..3 and C is negative, so the high-count tier strictly favors A for every finite B and m.
